test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 13th December 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

If I will meet / my friend today, / I shall give / him this book.
solution:
The correct answer is **'if I will meet'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is a conditional sentence where the first part is describing a possible event and the second part its consequence.
 
• The **'if' **at the beginning of the sentence makes it a possible event and not something that is sure to happen so **'will' **cannot be used as it is used to denote sure events.
 
• The correct structure should be **'If I meet'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• We use the first conditional to talk about real situations in the present or in the future.
 
• The structure: **If + Present Simple, will/can/must/imperative form + verb**
 
 
• Example- If you're free later, we can go for a walk.
 
 
• If you're hungry, I'll make some sandwiches.
